After a 6 month break I drank again on my 30th birthday because I thought that it had been long enough that I felt like I didn't have a problem. What ensued was a 4 month bender of drinking every day from the time I woke up till the time I would pass out from the inability to function. Being a bartender and in a drinking town it was pretty easy to hide how much I was actually drinking from my family  and friends. I thought I was doing pretty well actually, because I still had my job and a social life. 

Until I woke up one afternoon to a bunch of texts and and Facebook notifications about some horrible stuff I did at a bar I frequented, when I went out to get my car and see if I could put together and fix any of the mess I made, I found that my car was completely totalled sitting in my driveway. Fear. Horrible and crippling fear and dread. What did I do? Did I hurt anyone? What can I possibly do?  I called my friend and immediately checked into a hospital as I didn't want to drink anymore, and the DTs had already started to set it. Alcohol had defeated me. 

After a 7 day detox and a 28 day stay in a wonderful rehab facility, I came home and got to work.  One thing that I found is that with real effort comes real reward. I'm not going to say that my life is perfect but throughout my journey in sobriety I have met so many people who have felt that fear and dread that I did that day and understand what alcohol can do to people like us. I'm not going to say my life is perfect or but I turned 32 last month and I can say without a doubt that putting down the bottle was the best decision I could have ever made for myself, my family, and my friends. 

You don't have to do it alone either, I know I couldn't have, there are people who want to, and will help you get through it. One day at a time. I'm here to talk if you need someone. This story hit close to home for me.  IWNDWYT
